requirement:
> `Close a delivered search and record dependencies for snippets you used to
> justify your conclusion without an additional source read. search_id is the
> result's UUID and used is an array of its short entry tags, e.g.
> {"search_id":"11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111","used":["1"]}. Entries
> whose source you also read may be omitted; including them is harmless. Use
> used:[] when no entries qualify, including an empty search. Every delivered
> search must be finished before submission. The result is {search_id,
> finished:true}; no additional source is delivered.`
rationale:
The requirement fixes the MCP description text for the `finish_search` tool. Its only structural obligation is that the tool definition carries that exact description.

`crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#impl[Session<'_, D>/ToolSession<D>]/fn[definitions]` builds the `FINISH_SEARCH` tool definition. Its `description` string matches the requirement word for word, with only JSON escaping of the quotes. It covers all of these points:
- Close a delivered search and record dependencies for snippets used without an additional source read.
- `search_id` is the result's UUID, and `used` is an array of short entry tags, with the example JSON.
- Entries whose source was also read may be omitted, and including them is harmless.
- Use `used:[]` when no entries qualify, including an empty search.
- Every delivered search must be finished before submission.
- The result is `{search_id, finished:true}`, and no additional source is delivered.

The same item also defines the parameters schema: `search_id` is a uuid string and `used` is an array of strings. Both are required, and `additionalProperties` is false. The description names those fields consistently.

The `references` lookup shows this is the only `{impl}` site. It also shows one `{cite}` in `md/requirements/sdk/graph/search.md`. The impl marking is on the item that produces the description, and `definitions` is the root, so no other item needs a reference.

I found no structural gap, no ambiguity, and no `{fixme}` to account for. I did not assess runtime behavior, because the task limits this review to the structural check.
